title: Normalization of an algebraic dualizing complex over a local ring
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring, where $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal, and let $\Omega\in D(A)$ be an algebraic dualizing complex [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing]. Put $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$. There is an integer $s$ such that $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\kappa[0],\Omega)\cong\kappa[s]$. Consequently $\Omega[-s]$ is a normalized algebraic dualizing complex for $A$. Shifts use $(K[t])^j=K^{j+t}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: Put $B=\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$. This is a field since $\mathfrak m$ is maximal: for $a\notin\mathfrak m$, the equality $(a)+\mathfrak m=A$ supplies an inverse to its residue class. Thus $B$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $B$), and $A\to B$ is finite since $1$ generates $B$ as an $A$-module. Apply [lem-trf-finite-map-dualizing-transfer] with $L=\Omega$. The bounded-injective, finite-cohomology, and scalar-action hypotheses are precisely those of [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing]. The resulting $B$-complex $\Omega_B=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,\Omega)$ therefore satisfies all three algebraic-dualizing conditions over $B$.

source.place: Tag 0A7L (lemma-find-function), proof: the derived Hom is dualizing over the residue-field quotient by Tag 0AX0.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-algebraic-field-dualizing-shift] to $\Omega_B$ over the field $B=\kappa$. It gives $\Omega_B\cong\kappa[s]$ for some integer $s$ in $D(\kappa)$. Restricting scalars gives the required isomorphism in $D(A)$: the restriction functor leaves the underlying complexes, kernels and images unchanged, hence preserves quasi-isomorphisms and descends to the localization defining the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its value on $\Omega_B$ is precisely $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\kappa[0],\Omega)$ by the transfer statement.

source.place: Tag 0A7L (lemma-find-function), proof: dualizing complexes over the residue field are unique up to shifts; Tag 0A7M, opening paragraph.

proof.text: Use the Hom-complex model of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For a bounded injective representative $I$ of $\Omega$, [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective] ensures that $I$ and every shifted bounded injective complex are K-injective, so these Hom complexes compute derived Hom. Now shifting gives the bounded injective representative $I[-s]$ and $H^j(I[-s])=H^{j-s}(I)$, so finiteness is preserved. Since $\kappa[0]$ is in degree zero, the Hom-complex formula directly gives $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_A(\kappa[0],I[-s])=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_A(\kappa[0],I)[-s]$. Thus $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\kappa[0],\Omega[-s])\cong\kappa[s][-s]\cong\kappa[0]$. The scalar-action condition is preserved too: simultaneous shifting identifies $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_A(I[t],I[t])$ with $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_A(I,I)$ by reindexing and multiplying a degree-$n$ cochain by $(-1)^{tn}$; the Hom differential formula verifies this is a chain isomorphism, and degree-zero scalar multiplication is unchanged. Set $t=-s$. All three dualizing conditions and the normalization clause of [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing] now hold.
